collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The well is low and one family takes more than their share: speak to them privately, or bring it to the gathering.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The well is running low, and everyone has agreed to take only two pots a day. (subject) has noticed that (friend)'s family takes four, every morning, before anyone else is up. (subject) is angry, but (friend) has always been kind to (subject.him/her). What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) goes to (friend)'s hut. It turns out (friend)'s father is very sick and needs washing several times a day, and (friend) was too proud to ask. (subject) brings it to the gathering without names, and the village agrees that the sick get extra water. (friend) is grateful, and a little embarrassed.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) raises it at the gathering, by name. (friend) explains about (friend.his/her) sick father, in front of everyone, voice shaking. The village agrees to extra water for the sick. But (friend) does not speak to (subject) for a long time afterwards, and (subject) wishes (subject.he/she) had asked first.
